title: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
summary: Given a set of recipes and their required ingredients, along with a list of available supplies, determine all recipes that can be prepared.
statement: Given a set of recipes and their required ingredients, along with a list of available supplies, determine all recipes that can be prepared. Note that recipes can be ingredients for other recipes, creating a potential cycle. Return the list of achievable recipes in any order.
constraints: Each recipe has a corresponding ingredient list; recipe names may themselves be ingredients.
Supplies are initially available and cycles without an available entry point cannot be made.
Return every makeable recipe in any order.
hints: Availability flows from each ingredient to the recipes waiting for it.
Build reverse edges ingredient->recipes and an unmet count; process supplies with Kahn’s algorithm.
Decrement a recipe for each available ingredient; at zero, output it and enqueue it as a new supply.
A recipe reaches zero exactly when every ingredient is obtainable; cycles without an initial supply never enter the queue.
editorial: A recipe reaches zero exactly when every ingredient is obtainable; cycles without an initial supply never enter the queue.
